sections.h2: Selling a lakeside house in Coeur d'Alene
sections.html:
As the Kootenai County seat and North Idaho's biggest city, Coeur d'Alene occupies the north shore of the 25-mile-long Lake Coeur d'Alene, roughly 30 miles east of Spokane, Washington. Locals call it the Lake City or CDA. The 2020 census counted 54,628 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 58,179.

Downtown wraps around the water. The resort with its 3,300-foot floating boardwalk, the 165-acre Tubbs Hill natural area, City Park and Beach, and McEuen Park are all along the shoreline. A house a short walk from that strip sells differently from one on the outskirts. Say which you have in your photos and description.

Health care, education, tourism and retail carry the local economy. Kootenai Health is the largest employer in the county, and the Coeur d'Alene School District, with about 11,000 students in 18 schools, is the second largest. North Idaho College enrolls more than 5,000 students. Compare your loan payoff with a realistic net before you accept any offer, whether you bought long ago or recently.

January and December average 31.2 degrees Fahrenheit, and July averages 70.1. Temperatures pass 90 degrees on about 18.3 days a year, and a few nights fall below 10 degrees. Yearly rainfall is about 25 inches.

Plan around four items before a buyer's inspector arrives:

  • Roof and attic insulation, because winter wears hardest on older roofs.
  • How old the furnace or heat pump is.
  • Gutters, downspouts and drainage near the foundation after snowmelt.
  • Decks and docks, which face the harshest exposure on lakefront lots.

A cash buyer looks at the same list but accepts the house as is and builds repair costs into the offer.

Houses near forest face wildfire questions. The Idaho Department of Lands protects 9 million acres of forest and rangeland, runs an office at 3284 W. Industrial Loop in Coeur d'Alene and teaches the public about defensible space. It also publishes a fire restrictions finder, and state and county penalties apply. Anyone who violates a restriction and starts a fire is liable for suppression costs, including damage to property and resources.

If your lot backs onto trees, clear brush and dead material before showings. Ask the city and your insurer what applies to your lot.

sections.h2: Short-term rental permits end at closing
sections.html:
Under section 17.08.1030 of the city code, a short-term rental permit is non-transferable and valid only for the dwelling named in the application. When title transfers, the permit expires automatically. A buyer cannot step into your permit and must apply on their own.

The state also limits what cities can do. Senate Bill 1162 of 2025 changed section 67-6539, and a city or county can no longer adopt or enforce a rule that bans short-term rentals outright or in practice.

Tell buyers early that the permit ends at closing. Someone who counted on lake-house booking income will weigh the price differently than someone who wants a year-round home. Keep the permit number, booking history and tax filings in one folder.

sections.h2: Kootenai County property tax and exemptions
sections.html:
Kootenai County collects tax on Coeur d'Alene houses. Notices go out by the fourth Monday in November. The homeowner's exemption cuts a primary residence's assessed value by half, up to $125,000 beginning in 2021. The Property Tax Reduction Program takes applications only from January 1 to April 15, and you must apply and qualify every year.

EventDate
Tax notices mailedBy the fourth Monday in November
First half dueOn or before December 20
Second half dueOn or before June 20 of the following year
Homeowner's exemptionHalf of primary residence value, up to $125,000 (from 2021)
Property Tax Reduction ProgramApply January 1 to April 15
Appeal to Board of EqualizationBy the fourth Monday in June

A further appeal goes to the State Board of Tax Appeals or district court within 30 days.

Once your primary residence sells, find out from the closing agent how the year's tax was split and what happens to the exemption on the old house under the new owner. Hold on to the final settlement statement.

sections.h2: What a Coeur d'Alene seller discloses
sections.html:
Sellers of most Idaho homes fill out a property condition disclosure form. Section 55-2504 reaches anyone planning to transfer residential real property, rentals included. The form itself is set by section 55-2508, and section 55-2509 has the buyer sign and return it when one applies.

Exemptions under section 55-2505 cover transfers by a fiduciary in an estate, guardianship, conservatorship or trust, foreclosures, gifts to a spouse or lineal relative, and sales by an heir who has stayed away from the house for a year. If the house was never your primary residence, ask the closing agent which category fits.

Owners who value a fast, certain close over a long marketing period are the ones who call us. Examples from North Idaho:

  • An inherited house or cabin no heir plans to keep.
  • An older roof or heating system that would fail a buyer's inspection.
  • A former short-term rental whose permit ends at closing.
  • A move for work or family that sets a firm closing date.

Cash Home Buyers buys as is, with no commissions and no closing costs charged to you by us, and you owe nothing if you decline. Every house and payoff is different, so compare an offer with the net from a listing before you decide.

sections.h2: Pricing and timing around the lake
sections.html:
Where the house sits changes the conversation. A buyer eyeing a place near the waterfront is paying for the setting, so condition and presentation of the exterior matter. A buyer looking at the edge of town is paying for space and a lower entry price, so the roof, heat and drainage take center stage in the inspection.

Winter listings reach fewer buyers, and snow can hide roof and yard problems that surface in spring. If your timeline is tight because of a move, a job or an estate, a direct offer lets you pick the closing date without staging the house for showings. If you can wait through a full marketing season, a listing may reach more buyers. Weigh the two with your payoff in front of you.

sections.h2: Preparing to sell, step by step
sections.html:
1. Decide how to describe the location: walkable to the waterfront, lakefront, or an edge-of-town lot.
  2. Have the roof and heating system looked at, and clear brush if the lot touches forest.
  3. Find your county tax notice and check that both halves are paid.
  4. Gather the short-term rental permit number, booking history and tax filings if you rented the house.
  5. Ask the closing agent which disclosure category applies.

With that done, a listing and a direct offer can be compared using real numbers.

faqs.q: What county is Coeur d'Alene in?
faqs.a: Coeur d'Alene is the county seat of Kootenai County, Idaho.

faqs.q: When are Kootenai County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due on or before December 20 and the second half on or before June 20 of the following year. Notices are mailed by the fourth Monday in November.

faqs.q: Does a short-term rental permit transfer when I sell my Coeur d'Alene house?
faqs.a: No. The city code says the permit is non-transferable and expires automatically when title transfers, so the buyer must apply for a new one.

faqs.q: Is there a homeowner's exemption in Kootenai County?
faqs.a: Yes. It reduces a primary residence's assessed value by half, up to $125,000, beginning in 2021.

faqs.q: How far is Coeur d'Alene from Spokane?
faqs.a: About 30 miles. The two cities form a combined statistical area that crosses the Idaho and Washington border.
